answer: Each agent can bond tokens in a lagoon-style registry, with one bond locked per identity before it may submit bids or claim rewards. A randomly selected island of independent validators checks whether its work meets the task’s acceptance rule; failed or duplicate claims forfeit part of the bond. An attacker can still create many identities, but must lock real capital for each and risks losing it, so flooding the market with fake agents becomes costly rather than free. The plume of linked claims also gives validators evidence for detecting coordinated submissions.
